_why: PLA-8 batch 24 (alliums). Ids PINNED BEFORE FAN-OUT. Decided against the live roster with the CORRECTED stemmed scan (the batch-23 stemmer turned `beetles` into `beetl` and missed a real pair; this one strips a trailing plural `s`) plus a taxon check read from each crop's own prose. Authoring agents MUST use these verbatim.
_premise: SCHEMA-SPLIT BATCH. chives is FULL-schema (symptoms_*/cause_*/organic_treatment_*/prevention_*) and carries NO severity. leek, onion and shallot use the allium-only identification_*/management_* schema and ALL carry severity. Measured roster-wide: identification/management is used by exactly 5 crops, all alliums (garlic, leek, onion, shallot, spring-onion), and garlic + spring-onion are already laddered from it, so the method is proven for this shape. All 27 problems carry NO type at all (the batch 20/21 shape, NOT roots' coarse->fine upgrade). SCHEMA-AWARE COMPARISON IS MANDATORY IN THIS BATCH: any cross-crop prose comparison must use the field set the crop actually carries, or it compares None to None and reports identity. That is the defect that produced the retracted _twins claim.
_twins: CORRECTED 2026-09-02 -- THE ORIGINAL CLAIM IN THIS FIELD WAS FALSE. It said 3 template twins existed against spring-onion (onion/Onion thrips, onion/Fusarium basal rot, shallot/Onion thrips). There are ZERO. The scan compared the 8 FULL-schema fields (symptoms_*, organic_treatment_*, prevention_*) on crops that DO NOT CARRY THEM: leek, onion and shallot use identification_*/management_*, so 6 of the 8 compared fields were None on BOTH sides and the tuples matched on ABSENCE. Re-measured on the fields these crops actually have (identification_*, management_*, cause_*): all three share ONLY cause_beginner and cause_seasoned and DIFFER on both management fields, which is where a ladder comes from. TWO AUTHORING AGENTS INDEPENDENTLY REFUSED THE COPY INSTRUCTION AND MEASURED INSTEAD, and had they complied it would have shipped two defects: onion/onion-thrips would have DROPPED reflective_mulch, a control onion's prose names and spring-onion's does not, and onion/fusarium-basal-rot would have carried the word 'scallion' into the onion record. The real management relative is GARLIC, not spring-onion: onion/Onion thrips' management_seasoned is byte-identical to garlic's. Batch 22's check_template_sibling_divergence is therefore NOT armed for this batch on a spring-onion axis; any divergence guard must be re-derived per schema.

pests.name: Onion thrips
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM, live on garlic + spring-onion, roster-unanimous type insect.

pests.name: Allium leafminer
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM, live on spring-onion. Phytomyza gymnostoma.

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.evidence: EXACT-STEM x32, roster-unanimous fungal. NOTE the roster treats `downy-mildew` as a PROBLEM-CLASS id, not a species id: chives and shallot name Peronospora destructor while spinach names P. effusa and the cucurbits a different genus again. Reuse follows the established convention KNOWINGLY, not by oversight.

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.evidence: No bare `rust` id exists; every live rust is crop-prefixed (garlic-rust, bee-balm-rust, sunflower-rust, fig-rust, elderberry-rust, asparagus-rust). chives' prose names Puccinia rust fungi, as garlic's does.

diseases.name: White rot
diseases.evidence: TAXON CHECK PASSES: chives, leek, shallot, garlic and spring-onion ALL name Sclerotium cepivorum (leek gives the current name Stromatinia cepivora). Allium-specific, one organism.

diseases.name: Botrytis (leaf blight and neck rot)
diseases.evidence: Live `botrytis-neck-rot` is specifically the STORAGE rot: onion, shallot and garlic all describe infection of immature or insufficiently cured NECKS. chives' entry is compound in its own name and its cause describes a FOLIAR blight (dense canopies, splashing water, leaf wetness). The shorter id would name a narrower problem.

pests.name: Leek moth
pests.evidence: Acrolepiopsis assectella. No stem relative on the roster.

pests.name: Allium leaf miner
pests.evidence: THE SCAN SCORED THIS NOVEL AND IT IS NOT. leek spells it 'leaf miner' (two words) where chives, shallot and spring-onion spell it 'leafminer', so the stem key differs. Both records name Phytomyza gymnostoma: ONE insect. Minting off the spelling would have put two ids on one taxon.

diseases.name: Leek rust
diseases.evidence: Puccinia porri (formerly P. allii). Crop-prefixed per the roster's rust convention.

diseases.name: White rot
diseases.evidence: Sclerotium cepivorum, same organism as the other four alliums.

diseases.name: Pink root
diseases.evidence: No stem relative. onion and shallot name Setophoma terrestris; leek's prose says only 'a soilborne fungus' but describes the same disease in the same words otherwise, so all three share the id.

pests.name: Onion thrips
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM. NOTE: this problem is a TEMPLATE TWIN of spring-onion's, byte-identical across all its prose fields.

diseases.name: Botrytis neck rot
diseases.evidence: EXACT-STEM, live on garlic + spring-onion; the same neck/storage rot.

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.evidence: Peronospora destructor; problem-class id, see chives.
